editorial.meta_description: The NCE is a 200-question exam from the NBCC used for counselor licensure, covering professional practice, clinical focus, and various counseling skills.
editorial.overview: The National Counselor Examination (NCE) is a 200-question assessment administered by the National Board for Certified Counselors (NBCC). It evaluates the knowledge and skills required for entry-level counseling practice. Many states use this examination as a requirement for professional counselor licensure. The exam covers various core curriculum areas and work behaviors identified through national job analysis. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency across these domains to achieve certification and meet the standards set by the board for professional practice in the field, ensuring they are prepared for the diverse challenges of the counseling profession.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is for individuals seeking counselor licensure or National Certified Counselor (NCC) certification. Candidates must hold a graduate-level degree from a counseling program accredited by CACREP or an institutionally accredited college or university to be eligible for the examination.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the core CACREP curriculum areas and the work behaviors defined by the NBCC. Use the official candidate handbook to understand the 200-question format. Practice with the sample questions provided in the handbook. Ensure you understand the testing requirements for either in-person or online administration. Confirm your eligibility and test authorization window with your state licensing board before scheduling your appointment to ensure you are prepared for the testing day. Allocate sufficient time to master the content across all six domains.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers professional functioning, including the history of the profession, counselor roles, organizational structures, ethical standards, and the credentialing process. Candidates must understand how these professional standards guide daily practice and ensure the delivery of ethical services to all clients.

This domain focuses on the processes of intake, assessment, and diagnosis within a counseling context. It requires candidates to demonstrate proficiency in gathering client information, identifying presenting problems, and applying diagnostic criteria to inform the development of appropriate treatment strategies for diverse client populations.

This domain addresses various areas of clinical focus relevant to counseling practice. It emphasizes the importance of understanding specific client needs, developmental stages, and environmental factors that influence mental health outcomes, ensuring that counselors can provide targeted support and interventions tailored to the unique circumstances.

This domain involves the development and implementation of treatment plans for counseling clients. Candidates must show they can translate diagnostic findings into actionable goals, select appropriate therapeutic modalities, and monitor client progress over time to ensure that the counseling process remains focused, structured, and responsive.

This domain covers the specific skills and interventions used during counseling and consultation sessions. It focuses on the application of evidence-based techniques, communication strategies, and therapeutic approaches that facilitate positive change, helping counselors build working alliances and effectively address the complex emotional and behavioral challenges presented.

This domain focuses on the core attributes and qualities necessary for effective counseling. It highlights the importance of empathy, genuineness, and unconditional positive regard in the helping relationship, which are used for fostering trust, encouraging client self-exploration, and promoting personal growth throughout the therapeutic process.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at your test center or log in for your online session early. Bring valid, unexpired identification. Follow all security protocols, including the prohibition of personal items and electronic devices in the testing area to maintain the integrity of the examination process.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The examination consists of 200 multiple-choice questions. A portion are scored to determine if a candidate meets the passing criteria, while the remaining items are unscored field-test questions used for future examination development and ensuring the continued validity and reliability of the assessment tool.

The passing score for the examination is determined through a standard-setting process. Candidates must surpass the minimum criterion score established for the specific form of the examination they are taking, ensuring that all certified counselors meet a consistent level of professional competency required for safe and effective practice.

The total test session is 225 minutes. This duration is designed to provide candidates with sufficient time to complete all sections of the assessment. It is important to manage your time effectively during the session to ensure that you have the opportunity to answer every question presented.

faq.question_title: Where can I find my test authorization?
faq.answer_text: After registering with the Center for Credentialing & Education (CCE), you will receive an Authorization to Test email. This email contains your candidate identification information, which is required to schedule your examination appointment at an approved testing center or through the designated online proctoring platform for your convenience.
